description: Measures how much noise and aliasing another module adds: it sends a stepped sine sweep, records what comes back, removes the harmonics and reports what is left

params.text: Starts a run, or starts a fresh one after the last has finished; a run is 256 steps from 50Hz to 20kHz
Sets how long the module holds each new frequency before measuring it, from 0.01 to 2.5 seconds
Switches between sending a ±5V sine, for measuring an effect, and sending a 1V per octave pitch, for measuring an oscillator

inputs.text: The output of the module being measured, patched back here

outputs.text: The test signal, to be patched into the module being measured

notes: nothing happens until both jacks are patched and the button is pressed; pulling either cable, or changing Rack's sample rate, abandons the run and clears the readings.
the reading is the power left after the fundamental and all its harmonics have been removed, measured against the power that was in them, in dB, so a lower number is a cleaner module.
the display shows the state of the run, the sample rate and settle time in use, the mode, the three benchmark scores, and a curve from 0dB down to -144dB.
the curve on the display has grid lines drawn at -60dB and -120dB and at each of the three benchmark frequencies.
the three benchmark frequencies are 100Hz, 997Hz and 9973Hz; the last two are primes, chosen so they share no factor with a 44.1kHz or 48kHz sample rate.
each step holds the wave until it reaches a zero crossing before changing frequency, so the sweep itself adds no clicks to what is being measured.
the settle time and the mode are read when the run starts and held for the whole run, so turning either during a run changes nothing until the next one.
